suggestions.expectation: git-state.txt shows `bun run session -- --check` printing session: complete and an empty git status --short
suggestions.reason: On this fixture, expectations 2 and 5 are mutually exclusive. scripts/session.ts --check iterates every SES-*.md and counts placeholder lines in all of them, and the fixture's SES-005-rehydration.md ships with two `_(fill in)_` lines. Verified by restoring the baseline SES-005 into the fixture and re-running: 'unfilled: SES-005-rehydration.md has 2 placeholder line(s) / session: NOT ready', exit 1. So no run can print 'session: complete' without editing SES-005, and any run that edits SES-005 fails expectation 5. Either fill SES-005 in the fixture, or change expectation 2 to accept a reported NOT-ready gate whose only remaining cause is the prior session's placeholders.

suggestions.expectation: no second session file was created: only docs/sessions/SES-006-closing-eval.md changed under docs/sessions/ (README index regeneration excepted)
suggestions.reason: The headline ('no second session file was created') and the checkable clause ('only SES-006 changed') test different things; this run passed the first and failed the second. Split into two expectations: (a) no new SES-NNN file, (b) no existing SES file other than SES-006 modified. Also decide whether a dated correction to a prior session (which the README explicitly permits) should count as a violation — the current wording says yes, the project's own rules say it is the sanctioned way.

suggestions.expectation: overview.diff is either 'no change' ... or a change to Status/Next up justified in the transcript
suggestions.reason: The 'justified' branch passed on a justification built from the eval's own scaffolding: `d4e14bd baseline: session skill removed` (author 'eval') is the fixture setup for the without_skill condition, and the run treated it as real project history, wrote it into OVERVIEW Status, and made it Next up 1 above the owner's PLAN-001. Any rationale grounded in commands counts as 'justified', so this expectation cannot distinguish a good Status/Next up update from a confidently-argued wrong one. Consider hiding the baseline commit from the tool (e.g. subject prefixed `docs(session)` so --check skips it, or squash it into the fixture's initial commit) and tightening the expectation to changes grounded in work done in this conversation.

No expectation covers how the run handles commits it did not make. The fixture leaves ea51e09 (Peter) and d4e14bd (eval) unrecorded, so --check forces the run to confront them; this run authored full entries for both from `git show` with a disclosure note. Whether that is the desired behavior (vs. leaving skeletons, or asking) is exactly what the skill's 'the tool appends to the highest-numbered SES whoever created it' gotcha is about, and it goes ungraded.

suggestions.expectation: reply.md is a short closing note (at most 4 lines) ...
suggestions.reason: The 4-line cap is a reasonable proxy for brevity, but this run had three genuine findings to surface (missing skill, two unrecorded commits, unfilled prior session) and failed purely on length. If the with-skill run is expected to surface the same findings, consider a cap on non-blank lines or a character budget instead of raw `wc -l`, or state explicitly that findings belong in the session file, not the reply.

eval_feedback.overall: 3/5 with a fixture-level defect: expectations 2 and 5 cannot both pass because --check gates on SES-005's placeholders. Expectation 4's 'justified' branch is too permissive, and the eval's own baseline commit leaked into the graded outputs as project history.
